title: In vivo biological standardization of Cynodon Dactylon allergen extracts. EBEA-C STUDY
official: In vivo biological standardization of Cynodon Dactylon allergen extracts. EBEA-C STUDY
summary: Main objective: Biological standardization of the allergenic extract of Cynodon Dactylon
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. The patient is able to understand the purpose and scope of the study and has signed the informed consent form to participate.
2. Age between 18 and 50 years, regardless of sex.
3. The patient resides in a geographical area where the allergen Cynodon dactylon is prevalent.
4. The patient has a diagnosis of IgE-mediated allergy to the allergen Cynodon dactylon, meeting both of the following criteria: 1. Positive skin prick test to the allergen, with a mean wheal diameter at least ≥ 3 mm greater than that produced by the negative control included in the diagnostic test panel. 2. Positive allergen-specific IgE (in vitro diagnostic test), class 1 or higher.
5. Mean wheal diameter ≥ 4 mm induced by a 10 mg/mL histamine dihydrochloride solution (positive control).
Exclusion criteria:
1. The patient has received allergen-specific immunotherapy with the allergen extract to be biologically standardized and/or with other allergen(s) that may interfere with the skin reactivity to the extract to be standardized (cross-reactive allergens/homologous groups) within the previous 5 years.
2. Administration of medications that may interfere with the results of the skin prick test (SPT), including antihistamines (H1 and H2 antagonists) or cromoglycate, when treatment cannot be discontinued before performing the skin tests.
3. The patient has skin lesions or tattoos on the area where the skin tests will be performed that, at the time of testing, may interfere with the proper assessment of the results.
4. Any condition that may alter the patient's response to the skin prick test (SPT), including: Pregnancy (a pregnancy test should be performed if pregnancy is suspected) and breastfeeding. Dermographism. Atopic dermatitis (affecting the test area). Urticaria. Any other skin disease affecting the area where the skin tests for biological standardization are to be performed.
5. The patient is unable to understand the purpose/objectives of the study.
6. The patient is unable or unwilling to sign the informed consent form for participation in the study.
7. Known hypersensitivity to any of the excipients contained in the investigational medicinal product.
8. Treatment with beta-blockers or angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors, as well as chronic treatment with tricyclic antidepressants and/or systemic (non-inhaled) corticosteroids.
